subject: Asterium: request for tenant-specific TTL scoping + sampled proof of deletion
messages:
From: Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@asteriumhealth.com>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sara.liu@asterium-compliance.com
Date: 2026-09-07T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant-level TTL carveout + sampled proof of deletion

Hi Ben,

Quick note from our security team — Asterium is preparing for an upcoming internal audit and we need a scoped answer for one of our tenants running regulated workloads. Two asks:  

1) Can Redwood support a tenant-specific TTL shorter than the global default for inference debug traces (we're asking for 14 days instead of 90) and how is that scoped in the product? We need a short description of the implementation (what is purged, what is retained for forensics, and whether the KV cache snapshots are impacted).

2) For the request above, we need a small sampled evidence pack showing proof-of-delete for one tenant (metadata manifest + deletion audit entries) and a short note on the retention/archival controls used to ensure deletions are irreversible. A redacted sample is fine — just enough to satisfy the auditors (no PHI).

Can you confirm feasibility and expected turnaround? We're trying to close this during our audit window (end of September).

Thanks,
Amir
Security Lead — Asterium Health

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@asteriumhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level TTL carveout + sampled proof of deletion

Amir — thanks for the clarity and the timeline. Short answer: yes, we can scope tenant-level TTLs and produce a small sampled evidence packet. A few clarifying points so we scope the deliverable correctly:  

- "Debug traces" can be configured per-customer and per-tenant; we treat these as ephemeral session artifacts and they are not part of committed model outputs or customer embeddings.
- If you move to 14 days we will purge session traces and KV cache snapshots older than that for the tenant; we will not delete immutable billing/consumption records required for accounting (we can redact/segregate those if needed).
- For the evidence pack we can provide: manifest (list of keys/objects redacted), deletion audit log entries (timestamp + object-id + deletion action), and a short explanation of the purge workflow and S3 lifecycle/plaintext scrub steps.

Marissa / Jonas — looping you in for the actual evidence pack and to confirm what we can include without exposing customer PHI. Target turnaround: 48–72 business hours after we get confirmation on the exact tenant ID and any specific exclusions.

Amir — can you confirm the tenant id (or a pseudonym) you want us to sample and whether you want us to include a KV-cache snapshot excerpt or avoid KV data entirely?

—Ben

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-07T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level TTL carveout + sampled proof of deletion

Thanks Ben — tagging in delivery checklist and constraints. Internal notes for evidence generation:  

1) Packaging: retention-matrix-asterium.csv (maps tenant -> artifact types -> TTL values), sampled-evidence-2026-09-08.zip (contains manifest.csv, audit-log-snippets.txt, deletion-runbook.md), kv-cache-snapshot-ttl-log.txt (redacted lines only).

2) Redaction/non-PHI rules: we will replace any user-identifying tokens with stable pseudonyms (user_0001) and remove any free-form user content from traces. Audit entries will keep object ids hashed and timestamps.

3) For irreversible deletion statement we will include: (a) confirmation that objects were removed from active object store (S3), (b) confirmation that we expired related cache layer entries and rotated eviction tokens, and (c) description of eventual consistency window (up to ~60s) and background GC. We should also include a short pointer to our CAIQ evidence bucket entry for retention controls.

4) Approvals: Need go-ahead from Legal if we put hashed object ids in a customer-shared packet; otherwise we provide manifest lines with types only.

Jonas — can you prepare the manifest + the audit slices and estimate the exact list of files we can hand off? I can assemble the artifact zip and confirm redactions.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Compliance Programs, Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-08T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level TTL carveout + sampled proof of deletion

Marissa — quick technical summary and what I can produce within 24 hours:  

- I will generate manifest.csv with columns: object_type, object_hash (sha256, truncated), created_at, deleted_at. For external delivery we will zero out object_hash and replace with object_token_xxx unless Legal approves hashed ids.
- Audit-log-snippets.txt: I will extract the deletion events from the audit stream for the sample window and redact IPs and user-agents.
- kv-cache-snapshot-ttl-log.txt: this is a short generated file showing eviction markers for KV namespaces; again redacted to remove keys.
- Deletion-runbook.md: step-by-step of our purge path (API call -> async GC -> S3 lifecycle -> manifest update -> audit emit).

Limitations to call out to Asterium:
- We cannot purge billing artifacts older than 90 days without an accounting exception; if you need those purged we will need a formal request from finance/legal.
- Forensics retention: if Asterium plans to request full-fidelity traces for litigation we recommend a temporary hold (we can support short-lived preserves).

I'll stage the artifacts to a secure Drive folder and provide a signed notice in the zip. ETA: I can have the package ready for Marissa by 2026-09-08T15:00:00-07:00.

—Jonas

Jonas Weber
Principal Engineer, Inference Ops, Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@asteriumhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, sara.liu@asterium-compliance.com
Date: 2026-09-09T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level TTL carveout + sampled proof of deletion

Amir — thanks for confirming offline that we should proceed with tenant_id: asterium-prod-12 (pseudonymized in packet). Per the plan above we've produced a small evidence packet and a TTL mapping file. Deliverables attached and links below:  

Attachments (redacted where indicated):
- retention-matrix-asterium.csv (maps artifact classes to TTLs and exceptions)
- sampled-evidence-2026-09-08.zip (manifest.csv [object hashes redacted], audit-log-snippets.txt [deletion events], deletion-runbook.md)
- kv-cache-snapshot-ttl-log.txt (redaction applied)

Notes / commitments:  
- We confirm session traces and KV snapshot artifacts older than 14 days for the named tenant have been purged in the sample window; the audit entries in the package show deletion events and produced manifests.
- Billing/chargeback records remain on a 90d schedule unless you request an accounting exception.
- If you require hashes instead of tokens in manifests we will need signed approval from your legal team; otherwise the delivered manifest uses stable object tokens.

Drive folder (secure, read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-asterium-evidence  
Ticket (internal): HBSP-43219 — assigned to Jonas for any follow-up artifacts.

If this looks good for the auditors, tell us if you want a short cover letter from Legal confirming our deletion workflow; we can route that through our legal team.

Best,
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs referenced above: retention-matrix-asterium.csv (CSV), sampled-evidence-2026-09-08.zip (ZIP), kv-cache-snapshot-ttl-log.txt (TXT)
